evidence.reason: The unsafe-metadata negative control mutates the drop-in to 0666, records `mutated_files = repair_files()` before the CLI runs, then runs the CLI. After the CLI it captures records, completions and units (lines 2372-2375) but never re-captures the fixture files; `cleanup()` at line 2376 restores `original_mode` before any assertion. Because the later preservation check sees the post-cleanup tree (which cleanup has restored toward the baseline), a controller that chmods the drop-in to 0600 and then refuses is indistinguishable from one that wrote nothing: the mode change to the fixture is undone before the files are compared. This is an implementation gap in the existing side-effect verification (records/completions/units are checked, files are not captured post-run), not a new requirement. Capturing `repair_files()` immediately after `cli_activators` returns and comparing it with `mutated_files`, with `cleanup()` in a `finally`, would detect the write.
